relations.note: Jimmu is his son.
Jimmu is her son.
Jimmu belongs to her heavenly imperial lineage.

relations.myth: Heavenly guidance during the eastern expedition
relations.note: She communicates protective guidance and sends Yatagarasu in the Nihon shoki.
He is an intermediate ancestor in Jimmu's heavenly lineage.
Jimmu descends from Ninigi through Hoori and Ugayafukiaezu.
Jimmu is his grandson through Ugayafukiaezu.
Watatsumi is Jimmu's maternal great-grandfather.
Itsuse is Jimmu's elder brother.

relations.myth: Eastern expedition and battle against Naga-sune-hiko
relations.note: He co-leads the expedition and advises approaching Yamato with the sun behind.
Inahi is one of Jimmu's brothers.
Mikenu is one of Jimmu's brothers.
She is Jimmu's pre-Yamato consort and mother of Tagishimimi.

relations.myth: Jimmu courts and marries the Yamato queen
relations.note: She becomes Jimmu's formal Yamato queen and mother of his successor's branch.
Tagishimimi is Jimmu's son by Ahiratsu-hime.
He is Jimmu's son and eventual imperial successor.
Kamuyai-mimi is Jimmu's son.
In the Kojiki, he is the divine father of Jimmu's queen Isukeyori-hime.
In the Nihon shoki variant, he is the divine father of Jimmu's queen.

relations.myth: Decision to undertake the eastern expedition
relations.note: He tells Jimmu of the fine eastern land and its heavenly descendant.

relations.myth: Reception of the expedition at Usa
relations.note: He receives and feeds Jimmu's party.

relations.myth: Reception of the expedition at Usa
relations.note: She receives Jimmu's expedition with Usatsuhiko.

relations.myth: Sea voyage and Mount Kagu clay mission
relations.note: He pilots Jimmu's expedition and later obtains sacred clay in disguise.

relations.myth: Battles for entry into Yamato
relations.note: Jimmu fights this Yamato ruler, whose forces mortally wound Itsuse.

relations.myth: Dispute over heavenly descent and legitimate tokens
relations.note: They dispute which heavenly descendant holds legitimate authority in Yamato.

relations.myth: Yatagarasu guides Jimmu through Kumano
relations.note: Takagi sends Yatagarasu to guide Jimmu in the Kojiki.

relations.myth: Ritual worship during the conquest
relations.note: Jimmu appoints Michi-no-omi to oversee public worship of Takamimusubi.

relations.myth: Divine sword revives Jimmu's army at Kumano
relations.note: He sends his land-subduing sword through Takakuraji instead of descending personally.

relations.myth: Divine sword revives Jimmu's army at Kumano
relations.note: He delivers the dream-disclosed heavenly sword that revives Jimmu and his force.

relations.myth: Guidance from Kumano through the mountains
relations.note: The heavenly crow guides Jimmu and, in the expanded chronicle, carries messages to enemies.

relations.myth: Encounter with Yoshino's local beings
relations.note: The fishing-associated local deity meets Jimmu, identifies himself, and submits.

relations.myth: Encounter with Yoshino's local beings
relations.note: The luminous-tailed figure emerges from a well and acknowledges Jimmu.

relations.myth: Encounter with Yoshino's local beings
relations.note: The tailed child of the rock-pusher meets and submits to Jimmu.

relations.myth: Elder Ukashi's crushing trap
relations.note: Eukashi feigns submission while preparing a hall designed to crush Jimmu.

relations.myth: Elder Ukashi forced into his own trap
relations.note: Jimmu's followers force Eukashi into the trap, then kill and dismember him.

relations.myth: Exposure of Elder Ukashi's trap
relations.note: He exposes his brother's plot, submits, and joins Jimmu's adherents.

relations.myth: Conquest stratagems and worship of Takamimusubi
relations.note: He serves as Jimmu's chief ritual and military agent.

relations.myth: Ukashi confrontation and Jimmu's courtship
relations.note: The warrior-retainer confronts Ukashi and mediates Jimmu's courtship of Isukeyori-hime.

relations.myth: Rival heavenly claims in Yamato
relations.note: Nigihayahi is another heavenly descendant already established in Yamato.

relations.myth: Nigihayahi recognizes Jimmu and submits
relations.note: He recognizes Jimmu's heavenly status, presents celestial tokens, and joins him.

relations.myth: Golden kite dazzles Jimmu's enemies
relations.note: It alights on Jimmu's bow and blinds the hostile army with radiance.

relations.myth: Defeat of the earth-spiders in an Osaka cave
relations.note: Jimmu's forces defeat the cave-dwelling group described derogatorily as earth-spiders.

relations.myth: Mononobe ritual service at Jimmu's court
relations.note: Later tradition magnifies Nigihayahi's son's ritual relationship to Jimmu's court.
